news.title: FBI IC3 Impersonation Scam: They're Pretending to Be the FBI
news.excerpt: Scammers are impersonating the FBI's IC3 center, claiming they've "recovered" your stolen money and need remote access or banking logins to return it. The real FBI never calls out of the blue, never asks for remote access, passwords, or fees. Hang up. Don't click unexpected links. Report at ic3.gov. If you gave access or money, call your bank and bring your computer in. *Source: FBI Public Service Announcement — July 20, 2026*

news.title: Daily Brief 2026-07-30: FBI IC3 Impersonation Scam Alert + HaveIBeenPwned Breach Check
news.excerpt: FBI IC3 PSA I-072026-PSA (July 20, 2026) warns of AI deepfake videos of FBI officials and spoofed IC3 complaint portals (ic3-complaint-portal.com, fbi-fundrecovery.net) targeting prior fraud victims via Facebook Messenger and Telegram. IC3 never messages first, has no social media, never charges fees, and never refers to paid recovery firms. Only genuine portal is ic3.gov — type it manually. Daily tip: Check haveibeenpwned.com for the June 2026 Stealer Logs breach (56M emails, 124M passwords added June 15). Visit haveibeenpwned.com, enter your email, and enable 2FA on any compromised accounts. Obtain method: Visit ic3.gov directly (type .gov address manually) and haveibeenpwned.com (free web lookup).

news.title: FBI Warns: Scammers Impersonating IC3 to Re-Victimize You
news.excerpt: Scammers Are Pretending to Be the FBI's Internet Crime Center to Steal From You — Again. You get a message: "We recovered your stolen money. Click here to claim it." The sender claims to be from the IC3 — the FBI's Internet Crime Complaint Center. They might even have an AI-generated video of an FBI official "confirming" it's real. It's a lie. The IC3 never contacts victims through social media, email, or phone. They never recover funds for you. They never ask for payment to release money. This is a re-victimization scam targeting people who've already been scammed once. What to do: Type www.ic3.gov directly into your browser — never click a link. If someone says they're from IC3 and wants money or info, it's a scam. Report it at the real IC3 site. *Source: FBI IC3 PSA — July 2026*

posts.title: Google Chrome 145 Patches Actively Exploited Zero-Day CVE-2026-2441
posts.summary: Update Chrome now via Settings > About Chrome; restart browser to apply version 145.0.7632.75/76 (Windows/Mac) or 144.0.7559.75 (Linux)
posts.truth: Google released an emergency Chrome update February 13, 2026 fixing CVE-2026-2441, a high-severity use-after-free vulnerability in the CSS component. Researcher Shaheen Fazim reported the flaw February 11. The vulnerability allows arbitrary code execution within the browser sandbox via malicious websites. No sandbox escape has been confirmed. This is the first actively exploited Chrome zero-day of 2026. Microsoft Edge and other Chromium-based browsers will receive downstream patches.

posts.title: Monitor NVMe SSD Health with CrystalDiskInfo to Prevent Silent Data Loss
posts.summary: Download CrystalDiskInfo free from crystalmark.info; run monthly — blue status = good, yellow = warning, red = backup immediately and replace drive
posts.truth: SSDs fail without warning unlike mechanical drives. Heat, write amplification, and low free space accelerate NAND wear. CrystalDiskInfo reads S.M.A.R.T. data showing total data written, temperature, error counts, spare blocks, and health percentage. NVMe drives should stay 40-70°C; SATA 25-55°C. Enable TRIM in Windows (enabled by default). Keep 15-20% free space for garbage collection. PCIe 4.0/5.0 drives need heatsinks for sustained workloads.

posts.title: Chrome 127 Adds Real-Time Anti-Tracking, Site-Level Ad Controls, On-Device Processing — Free Update at chrome://settings/help
posts.summary: Google Chrome 127 introduced three privacy features: real-time anti-tracking that blocks third-party cookies and tracking pixels before they load, site-level ad controls for per-site ad personalization settings, and on-device data processing that keeps sensitive information on your computer instead of Google's servers. Update free at chrome://settings/help or download at google.com/chrome.
posts.truth: Most people don't realize Chrome has been sending a surprising amount of browsing data to Google by default — every site visited, every click, every scroll. The new version changes that equation. Real-time anti-tracking means the tracker script never even loads. Site-level ad controls let you tell Amazon "no personalized ads" while keeping them on a news site you want to support. On-device processing means when Chrome analyzes a page for phishing or malware, the analysis happens on your laptop, not in the cloud. It's the biggest privacy shift Chrome has made since Incognito mode. And it's free — you just have to update.

posts.title: VisiPics Finds and Removes Duplicate Photos by Visual Analysis — Free at sourceforge.net/projects/visipics
posts.summary: VisiPics is a free Windows tool that finds duplicate and similar photos by visual analysis — not just file names or sizes. It spots rotated, resized, or slightly edited copies that other tools miss. Download at sourceforge.net/projects/visipics, install, add your Pictures folder (or any folder), hit Scan, then review and delete duplicates.
posts.truth: I see this all the time — a customer brings in a "slow" laptop with a nearly full drive, and half the space is the same vacation photo saved five times from WhatsApp, email, iCloud, and Google Photos. Windows doesn't have a built-in duplicate photo finder that understands "similar but not identical." VisiPics does. It looks at the actual image content, so it catches the cropped version, the filtered version, the lower-resolution copy. Most people don't realize how much space duplicates eat until they run a scan. I've seen 20+ GB freed on a single machine.

posts.title: Find any file instantly — Everything Search indexes your whole drive in seconds at voidtools.com
posts.summary: Everything by voidtools is a tiny free program that indexes every filename on your Windows drive in about one second and shows results as you type. Download the installer at voidtools.com (choose 64-bit for modern PCs).
posts.truth: Windows Search is slow because it reads file contents, not just names. Everything only reads the file table — it's the difference between reading every book in the library versus just checking the card catalog. Customers tell me "I can never find my stuff" and five minutes later they're typing "tax 2024" and seeing the PDF instantly.

posts.title: Microsoft Edge July 2026 security update patches 7 critical flaws — update at edge://settings/help
posts.summary: Microsoft Edge 150.0.4078.83 fixes seven vulnerabilities including remote code execution bugs. Open Edge, go to edge://settings/help and it will check and install automatically.
posts.truth: I see this all the time — customers come in with a "slow computer" and it's actually a browser that hasn't been patched in months. The bad guys know most people ignore browser updates. Edge updates itself in the background, but only if you let it. Closing and reopening Edge once a week is the easiest security habit you can build.

posts.title: Microsoft Windows July 2026 Patch Tuesday Fixes Record 570 Vulnerabilities Including 3 Zero-Days
posts.summary: Microsoft released its largest Patch Tuesday ever on July 14, 2026, patching 570 vulnerabilities across Windows, Office, SharePoint, Exchange, and Azure. Two zero-days were actively exploited: CVE-2026-56155 (AD FS elevation of privilege) and CVE-2026-56164 (SharePoint Server authentication bypass). A third, CVE-2026-50661 (BitLocker bypass with physical access), was publicly disclosed. Critical RCEs include CVE-2026-58644 (SharePoint), CVE-2026-58608 (Print Spooler), and CVE-2026-58631 (Windows Admin Center). Obtain via Windows Update (Settings > Update & Security) or Microsoft Update Catalog (catalog.update.microsoft.com). Enterprises should prioritize AD FS, SharePoint, and internet-facing servers immediately.
posts.truth: Microsoft July 2026 Patch Tuesday released July 14, 2026 per MSRC release notes; 570 CVEs confirmed via Microsoft Security Update Guide. Two exploited zero-days (CVE-2026-56155, CVE-2026-56164) confirmed in Microsoft Security Response Center blog and CISA KEV catalog. CVE-2026-50661 BitLocker bypass publicly disclosed. Critical RCE CVEs listed in official advisory.
